desc:
React Native payments and analytics integration connects your app to the services it depends on, from Stripe and in-app subscriptions to push messages and your own API. Ecom Swift LLC wires each one up safely, tests it in sandbox mode and documents how it works.

## What is a React Native integration?

An integration is a working connection between your app and an outside service. The app sends a request, the service replies, and the screen shows the result. Common examples are a payment provider, an analytics tool, a push notification service, an email platform and your own backend API.

Most of these services offer a developer kit, but the kit only gets you started. Real integration also covers keys, failures, retries, privacy and what the user sees when something goes wrong.

## Why do integrations fail in real apps?

The demo works on fast Wi-Fi with a test account. Real users bring weak signals, expired sessions, declined cards and phones that were offline an hour ago. If the code assumes every call succeeds, the app freezes, double charges or silently loses data.

Keys are another common weak point. A secret key placed inside the app bundle can be extracted by anyone who downloads it. A careful integration keeps secrets on a server or in a safe configuration, and gives the app only what it needs.

## How good integrations affect revenue, insight and support load

Payments decide whether people can pay you at all. A clear checkout with accurate error messages means fewer abandoned purchases and fewer support emails. Analytics events show which screens people use and where they stop, which guides every later decision.

Push messaging and email tools bring users back, and crash reporting tells you what broke before reviews do. None of these produce growth by themselves, but missing or broken connections make improvement hard to measure and hard to fix.

## What a well-made integration includes

- API keys stored outside the app code, with a plan for rotating them.
- Clear, plain-language messages when a call fails or times out.
- Retry and offline handling for actions that must not be lost.
- Sandbox or test-mode runs for payments, with results recorded.
- Analytics events named consistently for sign-up, purchase and other key actions.
- Push notification provider setup, including device token handling.
- Crash reporting connected, so errors reach you with context.
- Your own REST API connected, with typed requests and responses.
- Short notes on each connection for the next developer.
- Store-rule awareness, so digital goods use the platform's own purchase system where required.

## What we do

You tell us which services the app should use, and we confirm how each will work before writing code. We then add the connections one at a time, test each with sandbox accounts and record what we saw.

Basic connects one service. Standard connects up to three, including your own REST API, with offline handling and analytics events. Premium covers a full set with a sandbox-tested payment provider, push notifications and crash reporting, plus an integration guide and a handover call. We do not store your secrets in our files, and you pay the service providers directly.

## What to do, and what to avoid

**Do:**
- Create your own accounts with each service before work starts.
- Use test mode until every flow has been checked end to end.
- Name analytics events once and keep a short list of them.
- Decide what the user should see when a payment fails.
- Check store rules before choosing how digital items are sold.

**Avoid:**
- Hard-coding secret keys in the app.
- Tracking more personal data than you need.
- Adding several analytics tools that report the same events.
- Skipping the failure case because the happy path works.
- Switching to live mode before testing refunds and cancellations.

## Who this service is for

A founder who needs Stripe or a subscription flow working before launch. An app owner whose analytics, crash reports or push messages were never set up properly. A team with a backend API that has no mobile client yet and needs the connection built cleanly.

## What we need from you

A list of the services you want connected, repository access as a collaborator and developer access to each service dashboard, where the provider supports invited users. We do not need your passwords. Keys are handled through the safe sharing methods each provider offers, and we confirm the plan with you first.
